def: NVMe commands, completions and namespaces carried over a network transport (TCP, RDMA or Fibre Channel) instead of PCIe, using capsules instead of shared-memory queues and doorbells.
The transport-independent message unit of NVMe over Fabrics: a command capsule (SQE plus optional SGLs and data) or a response capsule (CQE plus optional data).
A host-to-controller NVMe-oF message containing a 64-byte SQE and optionally additional SGL descriptors and in-capsule data. Its arrival replaces the PCIe doorbell write.
A controller-to-host NVMe-oF message containing a 16-byte CQE (and optionally data). Its arrival replaces the PCIe CQE write and interrupt.
Host-to-controller data placed in the command capsule after the SQE, saving a round trip. Its maximum size comes from IOCCSZ in Identify Controller (16-byte units, minus 64 bytes for the SQE).
The definition of how NVMe commands, completions, data, queue creation and properties map onto a specific transport (PCIe, TCP, RDMA, FC). Each has its own transport specification.
The NVMe-oF model in which commands and completions travel as capsules between host and controller, with no shared queue memory or doorbells. Contrast with the memory-based model of NVMe over PCIe.
An NVMe-oF-specific command with opcode 7Fh, distinguished by the Fabrics Command Type field: Property Set, Connect, Property Get, Authentication Send, Authentication Receive, Disconnect.

The Fabrics command that creates a queue pair on a transport connection and binds it to a host (host NQN, Host Identifier) and a controller in a subsystem (subsystem NQN, CNTLID). QID 0 creates the association.
Fabrics commands that read and write controller properties (CAP, VS, CC, CSTS…) over a fabric, replacing MMIO register access.

The relationship between a host and a fabric controller, created by an admin-queue Connect and ended by disconnect, keep alive expiry or connection loss. All queues and per-controller state live inside it.
A globally unique UTF-8 name (at most 223 bytes) for an NVM subsystem or host, in domain-based (nqn.yyyy-mm.reverse.domain:…) or UUID-based (nqn.2014-08.org.nvmexpress:uuid:…) form.
The NQN identifying a host, presented in every Connect command and matched against subsystem allow lists. Linux stores it in /etc/nvme/hostnqn.
A 128-bit value sent in Connect that identifies a host across all its controllers, used for reservations. Linux stores it in /etc/nvme/hostid.
A controller in a discovery subsystem that has no namespaces or I/O queues and serves the Discovery Log Page, telling hosts which subsystems exist and where.

Log page 70h on a discovery controller: a 1024-byte header (GENCTR, NUMREC, RECFMT) followed by 1024-byte entries giving transport type, address family, subsystem type, port, service ID, subsystem NQN and transport address.
A fabric-wide discovery service that accepts registrations from hosts and subsystems, applies zoning, and gives each host a filtered Discovery Log Page with change notifications.

A mechanism by which each controller reports, per ANA group of namespaces, one of five access states (Optimized, Non-Optimized, Inaccessible, Persistent Loss, Change) via log page 0Ch, so hosts choose paths.

Host logic that presents one device for a namespace reachable through several controllers (paths) and selects among them using ANA states and an I/O policy (Linux native: numa, round-robin, queue-depth).
Admin command 18h and the timeout KATO (set in the admin Connect for fabrics) by which host and controller detect that the other side has disappeared and end the association.

The keep alive timeout in milliseconds, set by the host (in the admin Connect for fabrics). If no Keep Alive (or traffic, with traffic-based keep alive) arrives within it, the association is torn down.
The NVMe in-band authentication protocol (Diffie-Hellman enhanced HMAC Challenge Handshake Authentication Protocol), carried by Authentication Send/Receive Fabrics commands after Connect.
In NVMe/TCP, a self-delimiting message on the TCP stream that begins with an 8-byte common header (PDU-Type, FLAGS, HLEN, PDO, PLEN).
NVMe/TCP PDU type 00h sent by the host right after the TCP connection opens. It carries PDU format version, host data alignment, requested digests and MAXR2T.
NVMe/TCP PDU type 01h answering ICReq. It carries the controller data alignment, the digests enabled and MAXH2CDATA.
NVMe/TCP PDU type 09h with which the controller requests a range (offset and length, with a transfer tag) of a command's write data that was not sent in-capsule.
NVMe/TCP PDU type 06h carrying write data in response to an R2T, limited in size by MAXH2CDATA.
NVMe/TCP PDU type 07h carrying read data, sent without solicitation. The last one carries LAST_PDU and optionally SUCCESS.
Optional CRC32C over an NVMe/TCP PDU header. A mismatch is a fatal transport error that terminates the connection.
Optional CRC32C over the data of an NVMe/TCP PDU. A mismatch fails the affected command while framing stays intact.
The 32-bit Castagnoli cyclic redundancy check (reflected polynomial 0x82F63B78) used by NVMe/TCP and iSCSI digests.
NVMe/TCP PDUs (types 02h and 03h) that report a fatal transport error with a Fatal Error Status and a copy of the offending header, after which the connection is closed.
Transport Layer Security 1.3 protecting an NVMe/TCP connection, using configured or generated pre-shared keys. On Linux, the handshake is done by the tlshd daemon and the data path by kernel TLS.
Networking in which an adapter reads or writes memory on a remote host within regions the remote side registered and named with keys, without the remote CPU copying data.
A network adapter that implements RDMA queue pairs, memory registration, and RDMA READ/WRITE/SEND in hardware.
InfiniBand transport carried over Ethernet: v1 at Layer 2 (EtherType 0x8915), v2 over UDP/IP with destination port 4791 (routable).
RDMA layered on TCP/IP (RDMAP, DDP and MPA, IETF RFC 5040–5044). It tolerates lossy and routed networks.
A switched fabric with its own link, network and transport layers, designed for RDMA, with credit-based flow control and a subnet manager.
In RDMA, a send queue and a receive queue bound (for the Reliable Connected service) to one remote QP. NVMe/RDMA uses one QP per NVMe queue pair.
Pinning a buffer and loading its translations and access rights into an RNIC, producing local and remote keys. NVMe/RDMA hosts usually register each I/O buffer per command (fast registration).

A 32-bit handle naming a registered memory region that a remote RNIC may access with RDMA READ/WRITE. In NVMe/RDMA it travels in the Keyed SGL descriptor and is invalidated when the command completes.
SGL descriptor type 4h carrying a 64-bit address, 24-bit length and 32-bit key. Subtype Fh asks the target to invalidate the key (SEND with Invalidate).
The service that resolves addresses and establishes RDMA connections (REQ/REP/RTU/REJ). NVMe/RDMA carries record format, QID and queue sizes in its private data.
An RDMA NAK sent when a SEND arrives and no receive buffer is posted. The sender retries after a timer, and exhausted retries fail the QP.

The in-kernel Linux NVMe-oF target, configured through configfs under /sys/kernel/config/nvmet (subsystems, namespaces, ports, hosts, ANA groups), with transports nvmet-tcp, nvmet-rdma, nvmet-fc and loop.
